subject: english-language
title: Oral English: short and long vowels
summary: Hear the difference between ship and sheep, full and fool, for the WASSCE oral test.

lesson.text: English spelling does not show sounds clearly, so the WASSCE oral test asks which words share a vowel sound. The symbols between slashes are from the phonetic alphabet used in exam papers.
Three pairs that are often mixed up

items: /ɪ/ short: ship, sit, live, women, busy, village
/iː/ long: sheep, seat, leave, key, people, police
/ʊ/ short: full, book, good, put, woman, could
/uː/ long: fool, food, shoe, blue, juice, two
/ɑː/ long: cart, father, heart, half, calm

lesson.text: The same letters can make different sounds, and different letters can make the same sound. Look at "women": the o makes /ɪ/. In "people", the eo makes /iː/. In "heart", ea makes /ɑː/, but in "heat" it makes /iː/.

lesson.title: Which word has the same vowel sound as "seat"? sit, key, bed, set
steps: sit has short /ɪ/; bed and set have /e/.
key has /iː/. The answer is key.

lesson.text: Say these pairs aloud and make the long sound clearly longer: ship/sheep, live/leave, full/fool, pull/pool, cat/cart, hat/heart.
Listen to news readers on radio or online and copy how they say words. Saying words aloud beats reading them silently.

questions.prompt: Which word has the same vowel sound as "ship"?
questions.explanation: Ship has short /ɪ/. In busy, the u is also /ɪ/ ("bizzy"). Sheep and seat have long /iː/.

questions.prompt: Which word has the long vowel /uː/?
questions.explanation: Food has long /uː/. Book, full and put all have short /ʊ/, even though book and food look alike.
Heart is pronounced with /ɑː/, like cart. Hat has /æ/, heat has /iː/ and hurt has /ɜː/.

questions.prompt: In which word does the letter o make the sound /ɪ/?
questions.explanation: Women is said "wimin": its first vowel is /ɪ/. Woman has /ʊ/ in the first syllable.

questions.prompt: Which word has the same vowel sound as "pool"?
questions.explanation: Pool and blue both have long /uː/. Pull, good and could have short /ʊ/.
